newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Veba 96 profits increase, but growth to slow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Veba 96 profits increase, but growth to slow.

text.p: German energy to telecoms giant Veba AG on Wednesday announced a 25 percent gain in group net profits in 1996 and proposed a higher dividend, but warned that earnings growth would slow in the current year.
Group net profits rose to 2.63 billion marks ($1.6 billion) last year from 2.11 billion the year before on sales of 74.54 billion marks, which were up from 72.37 billion marks.
Earnings, based on German analysts' DVFA formula, rose to 5.04 marks per share from 4.33 marks, enabling management to propose a 20 pfennig increase in the dividend to 1.90 marks.
However, Veba cautioned that future growth would not match the pace of recent expansion, saying that a sluggish overall economic picture could harm earnings this year.

"Veba expects further earnings growth in the current financial year, albeit without the high growth rates achieved in recent years," Ulrich Hartmann, Veba management board chairman, told a news conference.

The lower earnings forecast hit Veba shares, which were down around 1.36 percent in afternoon electronic trade on the German stock market, while the IBIS DAX-30 index was up 1.69 percent at 3,432.13 points.
Hartmann emphasised that measures for enhancing productivity, portfolio optimisation and the expansion and internationalisation of its core business would help earnings.
As part of the process, Veba said it plans to further widen its shareholder base by listing on the New York Stock Exchange on October 8.
No capital raise was planned in connection with the listing and Veba said the U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs will co-ordinate the listing.
Joeri Sels, utilities analyst at WestLB Research, said the results were "softly disappointing" because of the forecast slowdown in earnings, but he said the NYSE listing was a positive development.
Among its divisions, the star performer again was Veba's long-standing cash cow, its electricity unit, with DVFA earnings of 1.45 billion marks on turnover of 15.3 billion.
"I am very positive on the outlook for the electricity unit" said Sels, who believed it would remain a crucial revenue source for Veba.

While the electricity unit continued to enjoy high margins, Hartmann was "extremely disappointed" with the performance at Veba's trading, transportation and services unit, where earnings fell to 370 million marks in 1996 from 430 million.

Earnings in its chemicals division were also lower at 460 million marks, down from 503 million marks a year earlier. It was too early to say whether its chemical unit Huels AG would be reporting a turnaround in earnings in 1997, Huels chief Erhard Meyer-Galow said.

With mixed performances coming from its existing businesses, Veba said it would continue the expansion of fledgling telecommunications business, which made start-up losses of 208 million marks in 1996.

It was in particular looking to build on its telecoms operations with its partner, utility RWE AG, through their O.TEL.O joint venture, which they founded last October and which plans in 1997 to offer telephone service to private subscribers.
Hermann Kraemer, head of Veba's telecoms unit said he expected the group's mobile telephone business to be profitable by 1999, while the group's fixed network would become profitable by 2002.
Other numbers for 1996 showed that group pre-tax profits rose to 4.44 billion marks from 3.84 billion, while net profits less minority interests gained to 2.46 billion from 1.92 billion marks.
Net return on equity increased to 13.3 percent from 11.4, closer to a targeted level for RoE of 15 percent.

Cash flow eased slightly to 8.54 billion marks from 8.57 billion. The group cut back investments to 8.78 billion marks from 9.72 billion, enabling the sum channelled into reserves to be raised to 782 million marks from 513 million.
--Frankfurt Newsroom +4969 756525 ($ = 1.685 German Marks)
